input.question: Why do my legs get itchy when I run and how can I stop it?
input.ground_truth: It's an allergic reaction. I used to have the same thing happen to me occasionally when I biked a lot (45 miles at a time). The condition, which can be quite severe, is called [exercise induced urticaria](_URL_1_) There are a few theories on how it happen. One is out of shape types' bodies aren't used to the physical activity and the new activity causes capillaries (the tiny blood vessels in your body) to open, stimulating nearby nerves sending an "itch" signal. According to the [wikipedia article](_URL_0_), it can be linked to dietary issues that runners (and others) have, as in they eat certain foods before running and this leads to the allergic reaction during exercise. It can also be caused by hot showers, "fretfulness" (i'm not sure what that means) or fever. Many people find taking an antihistamine before exercise helps (worked for me, after a few weeks it stopped), while others need much more extreme measures. Be careful, in rare cases it can lead to anaphylatic shock.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do my legs get itchy when I run and how can I stop it?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your legs are like a soft, warm blanket. When you run really fast, your legs get warm and start to sweat a little, just like when you play a lot and get all sweaty. Sometimes, that sweat and the way your skin moves can make your legs feel itchy, kind of like when you scratch your arm after it gets ticklish.

To help your legs not feel itchy when you run, you can try these things:

1. **Wear loose, soft clothes:** Tight clothes can make your skin itchy. Loose clothes let your skin breathe.
2. **Keep clean:** Take a shower after you run, so sweat doesn’t sit on your skin too long.
3. **Use a little bit of lotion:** Put a little bit of kid-friendly lotion on your legs after you wash them. This can help your skin feel better.
4. **Don’t scratch too much:** Scratching a lot can make your skin get red and feel worse.
5. **Drink water:** When you run, you sweat, so drinking water helps your body stay happy.

If your legs get really red, bumpy, or itchy all the time, tell a grown-up because it might be something that needs a doctor’s help.

So, running is fun, but your legs might get itchy because they’re working hard and sweating. If you take care of them, it will help!
